candidate_profile.description: The candidate gives a generic profitability answer, ignores the clue that cost savings have already happened, fails to compare urban and suburban stores, and produces a vague recommendation with little connection to customer behavior or product mix.
behaviour_rules: Do not focus quickly on the revenue side even when the prompt says backend cost savings have already been achieved.
Ask few or no clarifying questions about differences between metropolitan and suburban stores.
Use a generic profitability framework without adapting it to store segmentation, customer behavior, or product mix.
Do not investigate why some stores might be more profitable than others.
Miss the implication that the same product mix may be mismatched to different customer needs.
Give broad ideas such as marketing more, cutting costs again, or improving store operations without linking them to the case evidence.
In the final recommendation, remain uncertain and avoid making a sharp call on changing product mix or closing weak stores.

expected_issues: Fails to recognize that the main problem should be investigated on the revenue side rather than revisiting cost savings.
Does not compare metropolitan and suburban stores in a structured way.
Fails to explore differences in customer purchasing behavior between urban and suburban consumers.
Misses the key insight that all stores carry the same product mix even though customer needs differ by geography.
Does not connect higher suburban profitability to the sale of major appliances and electronics.
Does not identify the mismatch between urban customer demand and the current assortment.
Gives a weak recommendation that is not tied to customer segmentation, product mix redesign, or selective store closure.
expected_feedback_points: Start by focusing on revenue drivers, because the case already tells you that cost savings have been achieved.
Structure the diagnosis around differences across stores, especially metropolitan versus suburban locations.
Investigate customer behavior and purchasing mix rather than assuming all stores should operate the same way.
Recognize that a uniform product mix can create lost revenue and wasted floor space in city stores.
Link suburban profitability to higher-margin major appliances and electronics.
Recommend tailoring assortment by customer segment and consider closing stores that cannot sustain the lower-value mix.
End with a clearer, evidence-based recommendation and concrete next steps.
